previous_statement: The exact valid inference is ||h_n(Z)||^2<=b_n||Z^dagger dot Z||+C_prod*e||Z||^2: amplified adjointness and product defect give the first comparison, and boundedness of h_n gives ||h_n(Z^dagger dot Z)||<=b_n||Z^dagger dot Z||. Replacing ||Z^dagger dot Z|| by (1+kappa*e)||Z||^2 is valid at n=1 by node 1.1, but for n>1 it is precisely the unavailable uniform amplified-corner estimate identified by node 1.1. Neither amplified Ha adjointness nor amplified Ha product defect is an amplified norm axiom for the corner product. Thus no bridging argument from the allowed dependencies proves the all-n scalar quadratic; the correct repair is to restrict this conclusion to n=1 and record the missing amplified-corner theorem.
new_statement: Take kappa:=C_ca and e_sq:=e_ca as supplied by the allowed validated corner-algebra dependency through nodes 1.1.5.1--1.1.5.2. For every e<=min(e_sq,e_prod,e_adj), every n, and every Z in E_n:=M_n tensor S_P, amplified adjointness, product defect, boundedness of h_n, and the amplified corner square estimate give ||h_n(Z)||^2<=b_n||Z^dagger dot Z||+C_prod*e||Z||^2<=((1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e)||Z||^2. If E_n={0}, then b_n=0; otherwise taking the supremum over its nonempty unit sphere gives b_n^2<=(1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e. Thus the scalar quadratic holds uniformly for every n, including the zero-corner case.
